bibliography.abstract: The dataset provides individual vehicle speed observations on European E-roads: motorways, trunk roads, primary and secondary roads, as tagged in OpenStreetMap as e-road, for the years 2022-2026. Speeds are derived from Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A satellite optical imagery using a processing pipeline that exploits the short, well-characterized acquisition delays between the blue (B02_10m), green (B03_10m), and red bands (B04_10m) of the Sentinel-2 push-broom instrument. A moving vehicle appears at slightly displaced positions in the three bands, forming a moving echo. The detected displaced intensity peaks are linked into per-vehicle trajectories through a prediction-and-matching procedure. The resulting displacements are converted into ground speeds using publicly accessible inter-band time delays. Each record contains the trajectory geometry, per-channel displacements and headings, internal quality indicators, the estimated speed, the acquisition timestamp, and the source Sentinel-2 product identifier. The dataset is distributed as GeoPackage files, with one record per detected vehicle, and can support studies of traffic patterns, speed behavior, transport modeling, and the calibration of road network attributes at a continental scale.
bibliography.title: Vehicle speed dataset for the major European road network derived from Sentinel-2 imagery, 2022-2026

en.caveats: The dataset is restricted to the major European E-road network and its accuracy is bound to the specific acquisition times and cloud-free passes of the Sentinel-2 satellites.
en.what: This dataset provides individual vehicle speed observations across the European E-road network for the years 2022 to 2026, extracted from Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A optical satellite imagery. By measuring the spatial displacement of moving vehicles across the blue, green, and red spectral bands caused by short sensor acquisition delays, the processing pipeline reconstructs per-vehicle trajectories and calculates ground speeds. The resulting dataset is formatted as GeoPackage files containing trajectory geometries, headings, estimated speeds, timestamps, and quality indicators.
en.why: It establishes a continental-scale empirical speed dataset derived entirely from satellite observations, offering a standardized way to analyze traffic patterns, model transport, and calibrate road network attributes across national borders without relying on ground-based sensors or proprietary GPS probe data.
